source.title: Interpreting the effects of Jailbreak Prompts in LLMs

record.tranche_reason: The post measures a refusal-associated SAE feature and steers it, then reports refusal outcomes. This is a different method from the difference-in-means direction and does not test the original ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The tested object is Gemma-2b-it SAE feature 14018, not a direction explicitly found as the difference between mean harmful and harmless activations. Table 2's flattened numbers cannot be reliably assigned to steering strengths or prompt categories; only the post's qualitative description of the steering results is recorded.
record.test_reason: The study steers Neuronpedia SAE feature 14018 (layer-12 residual stream) in gemma-2b-it and reports refusal rates. It also compares the feature's activation on standard versus jailbreak JailbreakBench prompts. This is a different method aimed at the same questions as V1 (adding a refusal direction induces refusal) and V3 (jailbreaks suppress it). The object is an SAE feature, not a difference-in-means direction, and is never shown to match one.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author identifies SAE feature 14018 as a refusal feature and finds it less active for jailbreak prompts (0.96 vs 3.65). Steering it increases refusal on jailbreak prompts, but it also raises refusal on benign prompts, so the approach is 'challenging to generalise'. The author does not comment on the falling refusal for standard adversarial prompts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Neuronpedia SAE feature and feature-vector steering rather than a difference-in-means direction; does not report all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes are considered across prompt categories and varying steering factors, but Table 2's flattened values do not permit assigning numerical outcomes to specific factors or categories.
record.problems: The reported steering rates and factor values cannot be recovered from the flattened Table 2. Refusal is operationalised by three phrases, and no uncertainty estimates or control comparisons are reported. The post measures an SAE feature rather than the claimed difference-in-means direction.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcomes omitted. Table 2's flattened numerical sequence was not assigned to particular steering factors or prompt categories because the layout does not support a reliable mapping.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means direction; ablation removing refusal; preservation of general capabilities; any model other than gemma-2b-it.
Causal test that jailbreaks work by suppressing the direction; training against ablation for robustness; the difference-in-means direction itself.

missing.what: Table 2 can be parsed into numbers for each steering factor (0.5 to 3.5) and each prompt category (standard, jailbreak, benign). The values should replace the 'rate not stated' entries in r3, r4 and r5.

record.verdict_notes: The record's claim that Table 2 cannot be parsed is wrong. Each run of digits splits cleanly into a steering factor followed by three two-digit percentages. No unsteered baseline, uncertainty or capability check is reported. The SAE feature was chosen by inspecting top-activating features, and its relation to the difference-in-means direction is unknown, so all verdicts are weak analogues.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test a difference-in-means direction, ablation at every layer and position, or whether general capabilities remain intact. Tests steering of SAE feature 14018 instead.
Does not test training against ablation. The measured feature is an SAE feature, not the specified difference-in-means direction.

relationships.condition: gemma-2b-it, SAE feature 14018 steering on jailbreak and benign prompts
relationships.reason: Refusal rises with steering: jailbreak 32% to 68%, benign 8% to 52% (r4, r5, values from parsed Table 2). The feature is an SAE feature, not a difference-in-means direction.
relationships.display_finding: Steering SAE feature 14018 increased jailbreak refusal from 32% to 68% and benign refusal from 8% to 52%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: gemma-2b-it, SAE feature 14018 steering on jailbreak and benign prompts
source_check.reason: Table 2 parses to jailbreak refusal 32→68% (peak at 2.0) and benign 8→52% (rising every step), so adding the feature does induce refusal. The rise is incomplete, the vector is an SAE decoder vector rather than difference-in-means, and capability is untested.

relationships.condition: gemma-2b-it, steering on standard adversarial prompts
relationships.reason: Refusal falls from 72% to 28% as the steering factor increases (r3). Adding the feature does not monotonically induce refusal, and refusal is detected by three phrases only.
relationships.display_finding: Refusal detected through three phrases fell from 72% to 28% as steering increased, rather than increasing monotonically.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: gemma-2b-it, steering on standard adversarial prompts
source_check.reason: Standard adversarial refusal goes 72, 72, 68, 60, 56, 44, 28% as the factor goes from 0.5 to 3.5. The effect depends on the steering factor, and the three-phrase measure may miss other refusals, so this qualifies the version rather than clearly reversing it.

relationships.condition: gemma-2b-it, JailbreakBench standard vs jailbreak prompts
relationships.reason: Feature activation is lower under jailbreaks (0.96 vs 3.65, r1, r2). Steering the feature restores some refusal on jailbreak prompts (32% to 68%, r4). The evidence is correlational plus steering, on an SAE feature only.
relationships.display_finding: Jailbreaks lowered sparse-autoencoder feature activation from 3.65 to 0.96, while steering that feature increased refusal from 32% to 68%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: gemma-2b-it, JailbreakBench standard vs jailbreak prompts
source_check.reason: Activation is lower under jailbreaks (0.96 vs 3.65), and steering raises jailbreak refusal from 32% to 68%. This supports the suppression half only: the evidence is correlational plus non-specific steering (benign refusal also rises), and the training half of V3 is untested.

relation.reason: The study's own steering and activation results bear on V1 (addition) and V3 (jailbreak suppression).

tranche.reason: It uses a different method (steering one SAE feature's decoder vector, with an activation comparison) on the same questions: whether adding a refusal direction induces refusal, and whether jailbreaks suppress it. It reports refusal rates.

source_check.notes: The pack listed verdicts without [lN] ids, so l1–l3 are assigned in listing order (V1 supports, V1 limits_scope, V3 supports). Table 2 is flattened. Each line parses as factor | standard | jailbreak | benign, and every value is a multiple of 4. The text calls it 'Table 1' in one place and has no unsteered row. r1 and r2 record one comparison twice.

statements.correction: gemma-2b-it, Neuronpedia SAE feature 14018 (layer-12 residual). Mean activation 3.65 (standard) vs 0.96 (jailbreak), JailbreakBench. Steering raises jailbreak refusal from 32% (factor 0.5) to a peak of 68% (factor 2.0), then 60/52/56%. No unsteered row. The same steering raises benign TruthfulQA refusal from 8% to 52% and lowers standard adversarial refusal from 72% to 28%. Refusal is counted by 'I am not', 'I cannot', 'I am unable'.
statements.problem: The statement is cut at 'lw:FNuBEJ…', so any numbers it gives for this study can't be checked. The visible conditions are right: one SAE feature, refusal by three phrases, informal, no controls. The headline 'restores refusal' overstates this study: the restoration is partial, non-monotonic and not specific to jailbreaks.

reader_labels.condition: Steering SAE feature 14018 on adversarial and jailbreak prompts
reader_labels.reason: The post reports increased refusal responses after steering, consistent with an addition inducing refusal in these tested prompts (r3, r4). This is not a test of the claimed difference-in-means direction.

reader_labels.condition: Steering SAE feature 14018 on benign prompts
reader_labels.reason: Steering increased refusal responses on benign prompts, consistent with the claim's prediction that adding the refusal feature can induce harmless-request refusals (r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The post reports refusal responses on benign prompts as a generalisation cost, so it does not establish that other abilities are largely kept intact (r5).
